title: Portugal's Public-Debt Interest Burden and Repricing: Pipeline, Data and Two Papers

creators.name: Ribeiro, Diogo
creators.affiliation: School of Media Arts and Design, Polytechnic of Porto, Portugal

description:
Reproducible measurement of Portugal's general-government interest burden, and of how quickly a rate shock reaches it. The archive contains the analysis pipeline, the generated tables and figures, and two working papers built from them.

Paper 1, the interest burden. Reconstructs the burden from the harmonised Eurostat ESA 2010 record for 1995-2025, keeping national-accounts interest expense, the GDP-normalised burden, the average financing cost of the outstanding stock, the debt-dynamics rate, and the benchmark yield on new debt as distinct quantities rather than collapsing them into one effective rate. Publishes an exact two-factor decomposition of the burden change into a financing-cost effect and a debt-exposure effect, and a euro-area comparison whose eligibility rule, ranking convention and membership year are stated.

Paper 2, the repricing kernel. Asks what weighted average maturity does and does not determine about pass-through speed. This version frames the maturity-versus-refixing distinction against established Average Time to Re-fixing and ESDM risk-indicator practice, then quantifies the Portugal-specific approximation problem. Separating the stock into maturity-driven, reset-driven and retail-flow components shows that a published maturity statistic constrains neither the reset clock nor the share of a shock each instrument absorbs. The reported reset-timing alternatives leave the one-year sign positive, while weaker shock-loading assumptions reverse it. A behavioural channel is estimated on Portuguese retail savings certificates and reported as descriptive rather than identified.

Sources. Eurostat government finance and national accounts for the burden study; IGCP instrument-class series and the ECB Data Portal for the repricing study. The AMECO extension is configured but contributes no rows to this build, and neither paper draws on it.
notes: Reproducibility regime: live-source, not frozen-source. Code, dependency lock, manuscripts and every generated table and figure are versioned; raw and processed inputs are not, and the pipeline re-downloads from providers that revise their series. Guaranteed: determinism given fixed inputs (the estimation is seeded and reproduces bit-identically), drift detection through a committed checksum baseline over 30 generated artefacts, per-payload provenance recording source URL, retrieval timestamp, size and SHA-256, and a recorded retrieval vintage per release. Not guaranteed: that a later run reproduces published figures to the last decimal. Readers needing exact reproduction should work from the archived release for the version cited. See docs/reproducibility.md.
